# The importance of accurately reporting water-quality tests

During a typical inspection, an inspector will review the most current
water quality results - the most recent written results of all tests
undertaken to maintain the safety and reliability of the water supply.
If there is a water quality problem, it may adversely affect water
treatment measures that may be in place. If a water treatment plant
makes a dosing adjustment, it must be evaluated to determine that it has
been properly carried out. The water quality information will be
provided by the plant operator - the owner or manager $-$ and, if there
are anomalies, the inspector should escalate the problem.
